sections.h2: Where is the Wexford County Register of Deeds located?
sections.html:
Find the office at 437 E. Division St., Cadillac, on the second floor of the older section of the courthouse. Letters go to P.O. Box 303, Cadillac, MI 49601, and the telephone is (231) 779-9455. The main entrance and parking lot sit behind the building.

Directions from the county: drive east on Harris Street from downtown Cadillac, go four blocks, and look to the left. Cadillac is Wexford's largest city and county seat, though it had to win the title. The seat started in Sherman, moved to Manton in 1881, and returned to Cadillac after a countywide vote in April 1882.

Mailed filings are accepted when sent with the fees and a stamped, self-addressed envelope for the return. State law does not permit recording a photocopy, so the sheet you send must be the original with original signatures.

sections.h2: What fees does the Wexford County office list?
sections.html:
Every document costs $30.00 to record, however many pages it has. That number folds in the Michigan remonumentation fee and the Register's automation fee, and it has been the statewide figure since October 1, 2016. Cash, checks and credit cards are taken, and checks are written to Register of Deeds.

  • Tax certification, $5.00, is required on every warranty deed and land contract.
  • A discharge or assignment that covers several instruments adds $3.00 per instrument beyond the base $30.00.
  • A fixture filing costs $30.00.
  • Copies run $1.00 a page, and certifying a document is $5.00.
  • Name searches cost $5.00 each plus $0.50 per year. UCC searches are $6.00 a name, and state, federal, MESC or judgment searches are $3.00 a name.
  • A track index request is $50 an hour, or $25 for half an hour.
  • Emailing a request adds a $3.00 convenience fee.

The counter also sells fill-in-the-blank quit claim, warranty and mineral deeds and non-construction liens for $5.00 each. Staff do not draft legal papers or answer questions about how to word them, and the office suggests hiring an attorney for any deed.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax applies to a Wexford County sale?
sections.html:
The county publishes a table that splits each $500 price band into a state share and a county share. A single check payable to the Wexford County Register of Deeds can cover transfer tax, tax certification and recording together.

First three price bands in the Wexford County transfer tax table, as printed by the county
Sale price bandStateCountyTotal
$100.01 to $500$3.75$0.55$4.30
$500.01 to $1,000$7.50$1.10$8.60
$1,000.01 to $1,500$11.25$1.65$12.90

Each further $500 band repeats the same pair of amounts. The printed table ends at $100,000, so for a typical home price ask the counter staff for the exact tax before writing the check. An exemption has to be cited on the deed itself, drawing on MCL 207.505 for the county tax and MCL 207.526 for the state tax.

sections.h2: What must a deed contain to be recorded in Wexford County?
sections.html:
The county posts seventeen numbered rules with statute citations, and each deed is checked against them. The ones that matter most:

  • Names typed or printed under the original signatures must match the names in the notary's acknowledgment.
  • Each deed or assignment gives the grantee's street or post office address and the drafter's name and address.
  • Page one leaves 2.5 inches blank at the top and every page keeps a half inch around the other edges. Ink is black, type is at least 10 point, and the paper is white, at least 20 pound, and between letter and legal size.
  • The first line of print identifies what the paper does, such as a warranty deed.
  • If the deed claims survivorship, a certified death certificate or proof of death is recorded already or referenced by liber and page.
  • A court order carries the clerk's certification and seal.

Unplatted land adds two required statements. One says whether the right to make further divisions under the Land Division Act is being conveyed, and the other is the Michigan right to farm notice about nearby agricultural operations.

sections.h2: Does Wexford County accept electronic recording?
sections.html:
For most paper types, yes. Court certified documents and anything needing tax certification are excluded, so warranty deeds, covenant deeds, land contracts, their assignments, plats and condominium documents must still be filed on paper.

The county's e-recording rules give a processing window of 8:30 A.M. to 4:30 P.M., Monday to Friday, except county holidays. Payment goes by ACH under vendor agreements, and only fees set by state and local statute reach the county, while vendors can add their own charges. A submission that breaks the Michigan Recording Act can be rejected. A filer who violates the state's e-recording standards is cut off until further notice. Four vendors are named: CSC eRecording, Simplifile, ePN and Indecomm.

sections.h2: Were any Wexford County records lost in the 2024 cyber incident?
sections.html:
Yes, a small share. A cyber incident on November 5, 2024 kept the office from recovering under 5% of documents first recorded between August 14, 2024 and October 30, 2024. Anyone who sent papers for recording in that stretch is asked to call and learn whether theirs survived or must be recorded again. A seller who closed in those months should make the call before listing.

The online land records search is hosted through the county website, and the office says its holdings go back to 1864. Duplicate microfilm sits in underground storage in Grand Rapids. Once a document is recorded, anyone may request a copy for $1.00 a page. The office will fax prepaid copies but will not email them.

It also runs a Fraud Notify service that watches for recordings under a name or business name. Ask the office how to enroll.

sections.h2: How does Michigan law connect taxes to a Wexford County deed?
sections.html:
MCL 211.135 keeps a warranty deed from being recorded until a treasurer's certificate shows the prior five years of tax paid, which is what the $5.00 certification line buys. Any balance owed on the parcel therefore has to be settled by closing.

The Register's FAQ covers family situations too. If a spouse dies and both names were on the deed, bring a certified death certificate and the fee; no new deed is issued, because the office only records. A paid-off mortgage produces a discharge from the lender, not a deed. The county cautions that adding or removing a name affects divorce, borrowing, taxes and probate, and urges an attorney's advice first. Once the sale closes, the buyer has 45 days to give the local assessor a transfer notice (MCL 211.27a).

sections.h2: What does the Wexford County housing stock look like?
sections.html:
Forest dominates Wexford County, which sits in the Northern Lower Peninsula and holds much of the Manistee National Forest. Briar Hill, at 1,706 feet, is the Lower Peninsula's highest point. The Legislature created the county in 1840 as Kautawaubet County, renamed it in 1843, and it organized in 1869.

Census figures put the July 2025 population at 34,445, across 564.93 square miles of land with 16,924 housing units. For 2020 to 2024, 80.9% of occupied homes are owner-occupied, the middle value of an owned home is $170,400, and median household income is $61,085. Permits for 191 buildings were issued in 2025. Many parcels are rural, so the land division and farm notice statements above come up more often here than in a platted city lot.

faqs.q: What is the per-document recording charge in Wexford County?
faqs.a: It is $30.00, which includes the Michigan remonumentation and Register of Deeds automation fees. Warranty deeds add $5.00 for tax certification, and discharges covering several instruments add $3.00 for each.

faqs.q: Can a warranty deed go through e-recording in Wexford County?
faqs.a: No. Warranty deeds and land contracts need tax certification, so they go in on paper: the original, with original signatures, delivered or mailed with fees and a stamped return envelope.

faqs.q: Will Wexford County staff advise me on wording my deed?
faqs.a: No. The office prepares no legal documents and gives no legal advice. It sells blank fill-in forms for $5.00 and recommends an attorney.

faqs.q: How can I learn the owner of a Wexford County parcel?
faqs.a: Ask the County Equalization Department or the assessor for the city, township or village. They give the name on the tax roll, which may differ from the owner, and that name opens a search of the Register's records.

faqs.q: Do I get a new deed after paying off a Wexford County mortgage?
faqs.a: No. The lender sends a discharge, release or satisfaction of mortgage to be recorded. Your deed remains the one from purchase, and a recorded copy costs $1.00 per page.
